 Semi-truck stopped twice in Missouri
 By Bruce Guthrie - November 20, 2026 
 post 
 Home   >   The Nation   >   Semi-truck stopped twice in Missouri 
 Reading Time: < 1 minute 
 A semi-truck driver was pulled over twice by the same deputy in Missouri. (Courtesy Platte County Sheriff's Office) 
 PLATTE COUNTY, Mo. — Two stops, same truck, same oversized load, same deputy.
 A driver with an oversized load was pulled over in Missouri last month, arrested, and pulled over again after bonding out by the same Missouri deputy.
 According to a news release from the Platte County Sheriff’s Office, on the evening of October 27, 2026, a deputy in the agency’s Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Unit observed a tractor-trailer hauling an oversized load on Interstate 29, “during darkness, without warning devices and oversize load banners.”
 After stopping the rig for an inspection, the deputy found the driver’s Commercial Driver License (CDL) suspended and that he lacked an oversize load permit from the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT).
 Authorities say that the width of the oversized load was measured over 13 feet. The inspection found eight Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) violations.
 The Louisiana motor carrier and driver were placed out of service, and the driver was arrested.
 During inventory of the rig’s sleeper, warning devices and an oversize load banner were discovered inside.
 Authorities towed the rig.
 The Platte County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office sought an arrest warrant, which was issued by the Associate Circuit Court.
 Two days later, after posting bond upon his arrest warrant, PCSO said the same deputy saw the tractor-trailer again with its oversize load, this time with warning devices and oversize load banners, driving on Route 92.
 “Having knowledge a MoDOT permit had still not been obtained, the Deputy stopped and inspected the tractor-trailer again,” PCSO’s release stated. “The driver had now obtained a valid CDL but still lacked a MoDOT permit. 15 FMCSR violations were discovered. A court summons was issued while the driver was assisted with obtaining a MoDOT permit.”
